lessons.topic: Separable and inseparable verbs (trennbare und untrennbare Verben)
lessons.title: Separable verbs
lessons.summary: Verbs like aufstehen split in two: the prefix jumps to the end of the sentence. Others, like besuchen, never split.

cards.title: When do you need them?
cards.body: Talking about your day and your appointments is full of them: **aufstehen** (get up), **anrufen** (call), **einkaufen** (shop), **anfangen** (start). The prefix changes the meaning of the basic verb.

examples.english: I get up at seven.
The course starts at nine.

cards.title: The sentence bracket
cards.body: The verb part goes to **position 2**, the prefix to the **very end**. Together they make a bracket around the rest of the sentence.
cards.tip: In the dictionary they're one word: anrufen. In the sentence: rufe … an.

cards.title: Which prefixes separate?
cards.body: Prefixes that are also little words separate and are **stressed**: **an, auf, aus, ein, mit, zu, vor, fern, zurück**. Prefixes **be-, ver-, er-, ent-, ge-, zer-, emp-** never separate and are never stressed.

examples.english: I'm visiting my grandma.
We don't understand that.

cards.title: With a modal verb
cards.body: When there is a modal verb (können, müssen…), the separable verb stays **together** in the infinitive at the end.

examples.english: I have to get up early tomorrow.
Can you call me?

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Don't forget the prefix at the end: 'Ich rufe dich' means nothing without **an**. And don't split **be-/ver-** verbs: **ich bekomme**, never 'ich komme … be'.

examples.english: I'm cancelling the appointment.

games.explanation: an-, auf-, ein- separate; be-, ver- never do.

games.prompt: Match the verb and its meaning
games.explanation: The prefix changes the meaning of the basic verb.

lessons.title: und, aber, dann…
lessons.summary: Linking words make your sentences flow. Some leave the word order alone, others push the verb right after them.

cards.title: When do you need them?
cards.body: Telling someone about your day or explaining why you can't come: **Ich habe keine Zeit, denn ich arbeite.** **Zuerst frühstücke ich, dann gehe ich zur Arbeit.**

examples.german: Ich komme gern, **aber** ich habe nur eine Stunde.
examples.english: I'd love to come, but I only have an hour.

cards.title: und, aber, oder, denn: position 0
cards.body: These four just connect two sentences. They sit at **position 0**: after them the word order stays normal (subject, verb…).

examples.english: I drink tea and he drinks coffee.

examples.german: Ich kann nicht kommen, **denn** ich **bin** krank.
examples.english: I can't come because I'm ill.

cards.tip: Remember them as ADUSO: aber, denn, und, sondern, oder — all position 0.

cards.title: dann, danach, zuerst…: position 1
cards.body: Adverbs like **zuerst, dann, danach, später, heute, deshalb** take **position 1**. So the **verb comes right after them** and the subject moves behind the verb.

cards.title: Telling a sequence
cards.body: For your daily routine: **zuerst** (first), **dann** (then), **danach** (after that), **später** (later), **zum Schluss** (finally).

examples.english: First I go shopping, then I cook.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: After **dann** the verb comes next: 'Dann ich gehe' is wrong — **Dann gehe ich**. After **denn** keep normal order: **denn ich habe** keine Zeit (not 'denn habe ich').

examples.english: After that we're going to the cinema.

games.explanation: und, aber, oder, denn are position 0; adverbs take position 1.

games.prompt: Ich gehe nicht, ___ ich bin müde.
games.english: I'm not going because I'm tired.
games.explanation: denn gives a reason and keeps normal order (ich bin).
dann is position 1, so the verb comes second.

lessons.title: First, second, third
lessons.summary: Ordinal numbers give dates and order: der erste Mai, am dritten Juni.

cards.title: When do you need them?
cards.body: For dates and birthdays, appointments, floors and order: **Heute ist der erste März.** **Ich habe am zwölften Juli Geburtstag.**

examples.english: The appointment is on the fifth of October.

cards.title: How to build them
cards.body: From 1 to 19 add **-te**, from 20 add **-ste**. Learn the irregular ones: **erste, dritte, siebte** (and achte has only one t).

cards.title: Dates: der … / am …
cards.body: **Welcher Tag ist heute?** – **Heute ist der zweite Mai.** But **when** something happens: **am** + ordinal ending in **-en**.

examples.english: Today is the fourth of April.

examples.german: Wann hast du Geburtstag? – **Am vierten** April.
examples.english: When is your birthday? – On the fourth of April.

cards.tip: Written: der 4. April = der vierte April. The dot makes it an ordinal.

cards.title: Writing dates
cards.body: In writing, a **dot** after the number shows it's an ordinal: **3.5.** = der dritte Mai (day first, then month).

examples.english: January 1st is a public holiday.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'einste' or 'dreite': **erste, dritte**. And use **am** for 'on': **am** zehnten Juni, not 'in zehnten Juni'.

examples.english: The course starts on the first of September.

games.explanation: erste, dritte, siebte are irregular; from 20 add -ste.

games.english: My birthday is on the 15th of May.
games.explanation: After am the ordinal ends in -en: am fünfzehnten.

lessons.title: um, am, im…
lessons.summary: Little words for 'when': um for clock times, am for days, im for months and seasons.

cards.title: When do you need them?
cards.body: Making and moving appointments: **Haben Sie am Montag um zehn Zeit?** **Ich habe von neun bis fünf Unterricht.** One question, **Wann?**, many answers.

examples.english: The appointment is on Tuesday at 2 pm.

cards.title: um, am, im
cards.body: **um** + clock time. **am** + day, part of the day, date. **im** + month, season. Exception: **in der Nacht** (at night).

rows: am Montag, am Wochenende, am Abend, am 3. Mai
im Juli, im Winter, im Jahr 2026 (or just 2026)

cards.tip: Small to big: um (minutes) → am (days) → im (months).

cards.title: From… to…, since, before, after
cards.body: **von … bis** (from… until), **ab** (from… on), **vor** (before / ago), **nach** (after).

examples.english: I work from 9 to 5.
From Monday I'm on holiday.
After the course we're going to eat.

cards.title: Telling the time
cards.body: **Viertel nach drei** (3:15), **halb vier** (3:30 — half *to* four!), **Viertel vor vier** (3:45). **Wie spät ist es? – Es ist halb acht.**

examples.english: We're meeting at half past seven.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'in Montag' or 'am Juli': **am** Montag, **im** Juli. And **halb acht** is 7:30, not 8:30!

examples.german: Können wir den Termin **auf** Freitag verschieben?
examples.english: Can we move the appointment to Friday?

games.explanation: um for clock times, am for days, im for months and seasons.
halb vier is half way to four.

games.english: I don't have time on Friday.
